quotes.text: If something's important enough you should try. Even if … the probable outcome is failure.
quotes.author: Elon Musk

source.work: 60 Minutes (CBS News), interview by Scott Pelley ('Tesla and SpaceX: Elon Musk's industrial empire')
source.locator: Broadcast 30 March 2014; CBS transcript, Musk's answer to 'Then why try?'

quotes.verification_note: Reused from quotes-final e03. Re-checked 2026-10-04: normalised match on CBS's own transcript = True for the spoken form 'Even if you -- the probable outcome is failure'; the '…' removes only the false start 'you --'. The circulated version ('When something is important enough, you do it even if the odds are not in your favor') = False on the same page — it is a paraphrase of this answer and is not used.

quotes.text: Failure is only the opportunity more intelligently to begin again. There is no disgrace in honest failure; there is disgrace in fearing to fail.
quotes.author: Henry Ford

source.work: My Life and Work, in collaboration with Samuel Crowther (Garden City, NY: Doubleday, Page & Co.)
source.locator: Introduction, 'What Is the Idea?' (the same sentences recur in Chapter XIX)

quotes.verification_note: Reused from quotes-final e05. Re-checked 2026-10-04: normalised match in Project Gutenberg #7213 plain text = True. Ghost-writer caveat: written with Samuel Crowther, published as Ford's own account. The circulated 'Failure is simply the opportunity to begin again, this time more intelligently' is a rewording of this sentence.

quotes.text: The trouble with every one of us is that we don't think enough. We don't get paid for working with our feet — we get paid for working with our heads.

source.work: Impromptu talk at a sales meeting of the National Cash Register Company, Dayton, Ohio — the origin of the THINK motto he took to IBM; wording as recorded by IBM
source.year: 1911 (IBM's page says 1915, impossible for an NCR meeting — Watson ran CTR from 1914)
source.locator: IBM Heritage, 'The origins of THINK'; the same two sentences were printed in his lifetime in B. C. Forbes, America's Fifty Foremost Business Leaders (New York: B. C. Forbes & Sons, 1948), Watson chapter (Internet Archive americasfiftyfor0000unse; page not determined)

quotes.verification_note: Reused from quotes-final e24. Re-checked 2026-10-04: normalised match on ibm.com/history/think = True. New: Open Library search-inside finds both sentences in B. C. Forbes's 1948 book (published in Watson's lifetime) and in Belden & Belden, The Lengthening Shadow (1962) — book text not opened beyond the hit. Spoken, not written; no contemporaneous 1911 transcript seen.

quotes.text: I do not think there is any other quality so essential to success of any kind as the quality of perseverance. It overcomes almost everything, even nature.

source.work: Interview with Orison Swett Marden, in How They Succeeded: Life Stories of Successful Men Told by Themselves (Boston: Lothrop Publishing Co.)
source.locator: Chapter 'John D. Rockefeller', Rockefeller's quoted answer to the interviewer; p. 206 (±1, from the OCR page headers of archive.org scan howtheysucceeded00mardrich)

quotes.verification_note: New. Checked 2026-10-04: normalised match in Project Gutenberg #64059 = True, inside the chapter headed 'JOHN D. ROCKEFELLER' and inside the quotation marks of a reply that the paragraph introduces with 'I asked Mr. Rockefeller' (structure checked by offsets, not read out). Same sentence found in the 1901 Lothrop scan on archive.org. Note the usual circulated form adds 'that' ('I do not think that there is…') — False in the book; the book's wording is used. Published in his lifetime; Marden's interview, not Rockefeller's own writing. Not in his Random Reminiscences (1909, Gutenberg #17090: False).

quotes.verification_note: Reused from quotes-entrepreneur e07 (PASS there); image replaced. Re-checked 2026-10-04 on QI (21 May 2013): exact wording = True (5 occurrences, incl. after the citation of 'The Story of Walt Disney', 1957); 'Diane Disney Miller', 'Pete Martin', 'Saturday Evening Post', 'kick in the pants', 'Page 89' all True; QI's conclusion names Walt Disney and the book.
